summary: Iteration 26: Verified the RTSP Digest single-connection fix. All 40 backend unit tests pass (test_rtsp_discover.py, test_net_scan.py, test_engine.py, test_iter5_diagnostics.py) — including the new test_describe_reuses_connection_for_digest_nonce. New iter26 API E2E suite (5/5 pass) against running mediamtx v1.11.3 on 127.0.0.1:8554 confirms: (a) rtsp_describe returns 200 for /live, 401 for wrong password, 400 for root; (b) POST /api/camera/test with the root URL auto-detects /live, RTSP handshake step is false (400) but Stream path auto-detect and Video stream (TCP) are true; (c) POST /api/camera/test with /live gives RTSP handshake ok true; (d) wrong-password test returns ok false, hint mentions 401/password, video attempts still run; (e) POST /api/camera/connect with root URL results in state.connected=true and state.rtsp_url auto-fixed to end with /live, and GET /api/frame returns a JPEG. Playwright UI test: login admin/9xsecurity, force-change form handled with Temp123456, typed root URL into rtsp-url-input, clicked camera-test-btn -> test-result-modal shows Stream path auto-detect ✔ and Video stream (TCP) ✔, URL input auto-updated to .../live, video canvas showed LIVE frames with status 'Connected — live monitoring chalu hai'. Restored admin password back to 9xsecurity via POST /api/settings and disconnected/reset the stored URL to a safe placeholder. mediamtx and the testsrc publisher were left running as instructed.

Modal (test-result-modal) intercepts pointer events, so any UI test that opens it must explicitly click a Close/Band button before pressing camera-connect-btn. Not a functional bug but a testability note.

rca of the issue: Original bug: rtsp_discover.rtsp_describe issued the initial DESCRIBE and the Digest-authenticated retry on two different TCP connections, so the second nonce validation failed on servers that bind nonces to a connection (mediamtx, real cameras). Fix in rtsp_discover._rtsp_exchange reuses the same socket for challenge+auth-retry and only reconnects if the server closed after 401; also passes algorithm=MD5 when advertised. discover_stream_url now walks all vendor paths before reporting 'auth', and engine.probe_rtsp continues to attempt TCP/UDP/FFmpeg video after a 401 (FFmpeg handles auth itself), only surfacing a password hint when everything fails. All three fixes verified end-to-end against a real Digest RTSP server.
